walkthroughs.body_html: In 1951 Asch used a simple line judgement task. 7-9 confederates and 1 naive participant sat together. On critical trials, confederates gave the same wrong answer first, then it was the participant's turn.

Asch tested 123 male US college students. They believed it was a vision test. Each completed 18 trials, with 12 critical ones where confederates lied. The unanimity of the group put strong pressure on the participant.
Mean conformity rate: ~37% across critical trials. About 75% of participants conformed at least once. Around 25% never conformed. Most who conformed said they did so to fit in — classic NSI.
